A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAFE-NET research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on eight PDE benchmarks, optimizer comparisons, component ablations and Hessian spectral analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a domain-knowledge-feature ablation and a mixed-boundary heat experiment. Appendix D separately attributes its reproduced results to other papers.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1.4 changes the specified frequency initialization from iπ to ℓπ/k, with k=L for homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries on [0,L] and 1 otherwise. This is a limited boundary-dependent adaptation; the feature generator, normalization, single-hidden-layer architecture and optimizer schedules remain intact.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a forced one-dimensional heat problem with non-homogeneous, mixed Dirichlet/Robin boundary conditions. The original eight benchmarks remain. Clarifying spatial versus space-time dimensions does not add higher-dimensional coverage.

E2.justification: The main baseline set is retained. Appendix C.1.6 newly compares PINN+DKF and SAFE-NET−DKF with standard PINN and full SAFE-NET. Appendix D's quoted large-model results are not newly evaluated controlled baselines.

E3.justification: The new DKF ablation introduces a four-variant controlled comparison under Optimization Schedule (2). Appendix A.1.4 also revises the reported initialization setting. Existing training budgets, sampling and error metrics are retained; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1.6 adds a focused ablation isolating domain-knowledge features in both PINN and SAFE-NET across eight PDEs. The activation, feature-count, initialization, depth, normalization and spectral analyses already present in v2 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random initializations/seeds. The new experiments follow this existing practice. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and plotted results are retained. New results include a reported 15.6% average error reduction from adding DKF to SAFE-NET and, on the new heat task, L2RE of 2.11e-4 for SAFE-NET versus 3.06e-4 for RBF-P. Tables 23–27 additionally reproduce attributed literature results under different settings.

T1.justification: Definition 6.1 corrects the tangent-kernel formula to evaluate its first gradient at x′ rather than x. Appendix A.2.5 also revises the RBF mapping formula. The central idealized eigenvalue derivation is retained, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same accuracy, efficiency and implicit-preconditioning claims, including their numerical efficiency statements. Added dimensionality and smoothness wording largely makes previously stated applicability limits explicit.

C2.justification: v3 interprets DKF as supplementary, with benefits depending on information supplied by initial and boundary conditions. It emphasizes the idealized, early-training interpretation of Section 6. Appendices D–E add substantive qualifications about differing objectives, data requirements and the limits of cross-framework accuracy and cost comparisons.

D1.justification: Appendix B.8 defines the previously unspecified Navier–Stokes regions R1–R4. Appendix C.3 supplies the new heat task's forcing, boundary data, analytical solution and training protocol. Initialization documentation is revised; the existing software, hardware and data-source disclosures remain.

R1.justification: The introduction adds numerical-software and LLM-based solver context. New Appendices D–E substantially expand positioning relative to large PINN architectures, FNO operator learning and EPGP Gaussian-process methods, discussing their distinct objectives, spectral representations and resource requirements.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include localized explanatory rewrites, clearer terminology and cross-references, publication information, and new appendix sections rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout, extensively resizing and relocating retained figures and tables. Table 3 expands PDE abbreviations. v3 adds Figure 21, Table 20 and Tables 23–27; existing spectral figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The DKF ablation and mixed-boundary heat test strengthen component attribution and applicability evidence. Appendices D–E improve the explanation of comparison limits, and several definitions become clearer. These are useful incremental gains, although the revised boundary-scaled initialization in A.1.4 is not fully reconciled with the iπ description retained in C.1.3.
